paragraphs: Friend, here's what I take from this one. Before a single sword comes out, God settles who the army is counting on. When Israel sees horses, chariots and a bigger army, Moses says, "do not be afraid of them; for the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, is with you" (Deut 20:1). The same God who already carried them out of Egypt goes with them into this fight (Deut 20:4).

Now notice how much care is packed into these laws. Men who have a new house, a vineyard or a promised bride are sent home (Deut 20:5-7), and so is any man who is afraid, so that "the hearts of his brothers will not melt like his own" (Deut 20:8). A city far away gets an offer of peace first (Deut 20:10). Even the fruit trees get protected, with Moses asking, "Are the trees of the field human, that you should besiege them?" (Deut 20:19). I think this is a heavy passage, and the words about the nations God is giving Israel are heavy too (Deut 20:16-18). Still, even in war, the rules stop Israel from charging ahead without thinking.

So what do you do with that, baker? When you face something bigger than you, you don't count your own strength first. You start with who is standing beside you, and then you move with care. Papa Dorin spent years in the back of a drawer, and I can tell you the LORD was with me the whole time. And Moses isn't done preaching yet, so keep listening.
